content: 1.  \( Q_{\theta}(s, a_{1}, \cdots, a_{h}): \mathcal{S} \times \mathcal{A}^{h} \mapsto \mathbb{R} \)  — the value function that takes in a state and a sequence of actions (action chunk). In practice, we train an ensemble of Q networks. We denote the weight of the ensemble element as  \( \theta = (\theta_{1}, \cdots, \theta_{K}) \) .

2. \(\mu_{\psi}(s,z):\mathcal{S}\times \mathbb{R}^{Ah}\mapsto \mathbb{R}^{Ah}\) — the one-step noise-conditioned policy that takes in a state and a noise, and outputs a sequence of actions conditioned on them.

3.  \( f_{\xi}(s,m,u):\mathcal{S}\times\mathbb{R}^{Ah}\times[0,1]\mapsto\mathbb{R}^{Ah} \)  — the flow-matching behavior policy parameterized by a velocity prediction network. The network predicts takes in a state, an intermediate state of the flow and a time, and outputs the velocity direction that the intermediate action sequence should move in at the specified time. See Algorithm 3 for more details on how this velocity prediction network is used to generate an action from a noise vector.
